_comment: SUB/WAVE's own 'Remote' TTS contract (docs/custom-tts.md in the station repo): POST /speak with {text, voice}, the rendered audio comes back as WAV bytes in the response body. If you already built a TTS server for the station — Qwen3-TTS, F5-TTS, CosyVoice, XTTS, Piper behind HTTP — this points the call line at the exact same server with no second bridge. Set Endpoint to that server's URL; `voice` is whatever your server means by a voice, passed through untouched, exactly as the station does. The declared sample rate is a guess your server may not share — run Test voice once, and if it warns about the rate, edit sample_rate here to what the probe measured. No voices_path: the contract has no voice list, so the Voice box is free text.
